chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: If the fornicator is flogged, then flees after some of the hadd has reached him, is it obligatory that he be left alone and not brought back, just as that is obligatory for the muḥṣan when he has been stoned?
He said: “No. Rather, he is to be brought back until the hadd is administered in full.”
I said: Then what is the difference between him and the muḥṣan, while it is a hadd from the hudud of Allāh?

He said: “The muḥṣan fled from death, and he fled only toward tawbah, because he has seen death with his own eyes. As for this one, he is only flogged, so the hadd must necessarily be completed for him, because he is not killed.”

key_terms.التَّوْبَةِ: repentance; return to Allāh after confronting the reality of death
key_terms.الزَّانِي: the fornicator; the one upon whom the hadd for zina is being discussed
key_terms.الْحَدِّ: the prescribed legal punishment set by divine law
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنِ: the legally protected married offender subject to rajm in this context
key_terms.رُجِمَ: he was stoned; the punishment of rajm was carried out upon him
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is flogged; subjected to the corporal hadd punishment
key_terms.يُوَفَّى: it is completed in full; carried out to its full prescribed extent

ai.seo_question: If a person convicted of zina flees during the hadd punishment, must he be brought back?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal distinction in the implementation of the hadd for zina. If a non-muḥṣan offender flees during flogging, he is returned so the punishment may be completed, whereas the muḥṣan who flees from rajm is treated differently because his flight is understood as arising from directly confronting death and turning toward tawbah.
